aboutP1: I’m Ever, a software engineer, a tinkerer, and a Rust evangelist in Rome. I’ve spent my career around systems that have to work: platform APIs at Anritsu, a weather system for the Italian Air Force, ML workflows at Qi4M. The stack changes; the job doesn’t: understand the thing, then make it legible to the next person.
aboutP2: I care about the seam between design and engineering. A good API, a clear error message, and a page that loads fast are the same craft in different clothes. Outside Anritsu, most of my work is Rust and TypeScript: Axum services, Postgres data models, and Astro and Svelte interfaces. I’m currently building BERLi, a work OS built on Rust that brings projects, timesheets, and HR into one place.
aboutP3: I write about Rust, infrastructure, and design. Away from the keyboard I’m a lifelong Linux user, a home-lab tinkerer, and a reader with more books than the Reading page admits. I speak English, Spanish, and Italian. I’m happiest when I’m learning something new, preferably by taking it apart.
